summary: Verified same-origin WebSocket fix in useTimerSocket.js. The display now connects via wss://<host>/api/ws derived from window.location and never gets stuck on 'Reconnecting…'. Backend regression suite (5/5 pytest) still green. E2E Playwright run against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL confirmed: (1) WS URL is wss://osc-countdown.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws (same-origin, wss upgraded from https), (2) idle footer reads 'Waiting for CasparCG OSC (0.0.0.0:7250)' in amber, (3) with test_osc_sender.py running the footer flips to green 'OSC receiving', CH1 shows opening_titles.mov counting down and CH2 shows commercial_break.mp4 (amber at 00:17, will turn red <=10s per LEVEL_STYLES), (4) wall clock updates, (5) after sender stops, channel panels revert to IDLE with '—'.
action_items: Remind Pi operator to re-run `yarn build` on 172.16.50.150 so the new same-origin WS derivation is baked into the served bundle (source fix is verified in preview).
critical_code_review_comments: useTimerSocket.js correctly derives WS URL from window.location; REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is no longer needed for the WS and can be removed from the Pi build env to avoid confusion.
Consider adding an explicit 'connecting…' state distinct from 'reconnecting…' for the very first render, though impact is cosmetic (WS opens within ~200ms).
Backend still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown; migrate to lifespan when convenient.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend WS URL is now same-origin (window.location). Backend unchanged. When testing idle recovery, allow >5s after stopping the OSC sender because backend osc.connected uses a 5s threshold on last_packet_age. Channels revert to idle after 2s (IDLE_TIMEOUT) but the footer OSC receiving badge flips only after 5s.
rca of the issue: Kiosk footer was stuck on 'Reconnecting…' from remote browsers because the React bundle on the Pi was built with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8001, so the client tried ws://localhost:8001/api/ws which resolves to the remote user's own machine, not the Pi. Fix: wsUrl() now uses `${window.location.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:'}//${window.location.host}/api/ws`, guaranteeing the WS targets whatever host the page was loaded from (Pi LAN IP, localhost kiosk, or preview ingress). Mitigation on the Pi: rebuild the frontend (`yarn build`) so the new hook ships in the served bundle.
